thread:
maria: Opening a short design thread: proposal for checkpointed retry tokens + bounded 'owner' abstractions at the ingress gateway. Goal: make retries and resumptions measurable and space-bounded without leaking client semantics.

ken: Short summary of problem?

maria: We currently have a resume token that clients can use to continue a stream. However: 1) proxies keep in-memory state for live owners -> OOM risk for long-lived flows, 2) retries can spin up duplicate upstream sessions causing double side-effects, 3) observability around which proxy actually served a resumed stream is weak. Proposal: attach a small checkpointed token that encodes (token_id, checkpoint_seq, owner_hint) — owner_hint is optional and advisory. Gateway keeps a bounded owner-index (memory-first, spill-to-disk ring) keyed by token_id with TTL.

leo: Owner_hint sounds useful for debugging but advisory only? If owner_hint is falsified by client, do we validate?

maria: Owner_hint is only for sticky routing preference. We sign server-side owner assignments; client-provided hints are ignored unless verified by our HMAC. So clients cannot force ownership.

ken: How do retries interact with idempotency? We should not rely solely on tokens for side-effect safety.

maria: Agreed. Token model: checkpoint_seq reflects last acknowledged event. For safe (idempotent) retries we allow gateway to reattach to same owner when checkpoint_seq matches. For unsafe ops, gateway forces a new owner and issues a fresh token. We'll require upstream to advertise safety via `X-Upstream-Op-Safety: safe|unsafe` header.

leo: What about hedging? If we hedge to multiple upstreams, do we create multiple owners? That could blow up the index.

maria: Hedge paths are short-lived and don't become owners until one wins the race and is promoted to owner. We record promotion events in trace with `owner_promoted` span tag. Hedge candidates get ephemeral ids that are not persisted.

ken: Observability: recommend metrics `token_attach_rate`, `owner_promotion_count`, `owner_spill_to_disk_count`, `resume_attach_latency_ms` histogram. Add a log line when promotions fail due to GC.

devops-bot: alert-rule created: gateway_owner_index_spill > 0 for 5m -> paging group infra-pager.

maria: On GC: keep a soft cap N (default 50k tokens in memory). When above threshold, evict LRU into a small LMDB shard per-process. Evicted entries still allow resume but with slightly higher latency (disk+lookup). We'll expose `owner_lookup_source` tag in traces (mem|disk|miss).

leo: How to handle partial responses during handoff? If a client cancels mid-handoff, do we propagate cancel to in-flight upstreams?

maria: Yes—cancel semantics preserved. Handoff is a three-step switch: 1) new owner reserves slot, 2) upstream `resume` request sent with checkpoint_seq, 3) once acked, proxy swaps live socket and emits `handoff_complete`. If client cancels during any step, proxy sends a `resume_abort` to upstream and returns cancel ack to client. Tests must cover partial ACKs and timeouts.

ken: Edge case: simultaneous resume attempts for same token from two different clients (network flapping). Need dedupe.

maria: We'll implement a token-level mutex with short backoff + idempotent attach semantics. First attach wins; second attach receives `409` with `Retry-After` and a small delta to jitter. Add metric `resume_conflict_count`.

leo: Any latency SLO impact? Disk spill sounds risky.

maria: We only spill when memory exceeds N; normal path is memory hit. We'll SLO on `99p resume attach latency` < 200ms mem, < 1s disk. Canary in us-west2 to validate.

ken: Security: token signing and rotation. How long do tokens live?

maria: Tokens are short-lived by default (24 hours) and are rotate-able. Tokens include a revocation list hook. We sign with per-region key and rotate daily; rotation policy documented in the RFC.

leo: Rollout plan?

maria: Phases: A) server-only token emission behind flag (no handoff), B) metrics + traces, C) owner-index mem-only handoff behind flag, D) disk spill enable + small canary, E) enable dedupe + conflict handling, F) global ramp. Each phase has a rollback plan.

devops-bot: rollout-playbook created: /playbooks/gateway/checkpointed-retries (status: draft).

ken: Tests: unit attach/dedupe, integration disk-spill, chaos: leader restart during handoff, concurrency: 50 concurrent resumes for same token.

maria: I'll add tests plus a small perf harness. Putting design doc in RFCs: https://internal/redwood/rfcs/gateway/checkpoint-retries - feedback welcome. :rocket:
